title: Future work: local restricted attention for large inputs
description: To improve computational performance for tasks involving very long sequences, the authors plan to investigate restricting self-attention to a neighborhood of size r in the input sequence.

evidence.anchor: self-attention could be restricted to considering only a neighborhood of size r
evidence.quote: To improve computational performance for tasks involving very long sequences, self-attention could be restricted to considering only a neighborhood of size $r$ in the input sequence centered around the respective output position.

This is a concrete instantiation and evaluation of exactly the concept described in the gap. Paper 2 (Cluster-Former) does not address the gap—its clustering-based attention enables cross-window long-range dependencies rather than investigating local-neighborhood restriction. Since Paper 1 fully solves the stated problem of investigating local restricted attention for computational efficiency on long sequences, the gap is solved.

paper.title: Local Attention Mechanism: Boosting the Transformer Architecture for Long-Sequence Time Series Forecasting
paper.abstract: Transformers have become the leading choice in natural language processing over other deep learning architectures. This trend has also permeated the field of time series analysis, especially for long-horizon forecasting, showcasing promising results both in performance and running time. In this paper, we introduce Local Attention Mechanism (LAM), an efficient attention mechanism tailored for time series analysis. This mechanism exploits the continuity properties of time series to reduce the number of attention scores computed. We present an algorithm for implementing LAM in tensor algebra that runs in time and memory O(nlogn), significantly improving upon the O(n^2) time and memory complexity of traditional attention mechanisms. We also note the lack of proper datasets to evaluate long-horizon forecast models. Thus, we propose a novel set of datasets to improve the evaluation of models addressing long-horizon forecasting challenges. Our experimental analysis demonstrates that the vanilla transformer architecture magnified with LAM surpasses state-of-the-art models, including the vanilla attention mechanism. These results confirm the effectiveness of our approach and highlight a range of future challenges in long-sequence time series forecasting.

assessments.contribution_summary: This paper directly addresses the gap of restricting self-attention to local neighborhoods for long sequences. It proposes the Local Attention Mechanism (LAM), which uses an additive mask to restrict each query's attention to only the L nearest keys (where L = 4⌈log n⌉). The paper provides a tensor algebra formulation that achieves Θ(n log n) time and memory complexity, and demonstrates empirically that this local attention mechanism outperforms full attention and other efficient attention mechanisms (Informer, LogTrans, Reformer, Autoformer) on long-sequence time series forecasting tasks.
assessments.what_remains_open: The paper fully addresses the specific gap of restricting self-attention to local neighborhoods for computational efficiency on long sequences. However, the gap description is generic ("investigate restricting self-attention to a neighborhood of size r"), and this paper provides one specific instantiation (L = 4⌈log n⌉, applied to time series). The gap as stated is fully solved by this paper's contribution. No part of the gap remains unaddressed — the paper proposes, implements, and evaluates exactly the concept described in the gap.
evidence_snippets: Let L be a neighbourhood size (in our experiments L = 4⌈log n⌉) and let M ∈ {0,−∞}^{n×n} be the square matrix with M_{i,j} = 0 when i − L+1 ≤ j ≤ i and M_{i,j} = −∞ otherwise. Then LAM is defined as LAM(Q, K, V) = softmax((QK^T + M)/√d_q) V.

This mechanism exploits the continuity properties of time series to reduce the number of attention scores computed. We present an algorithm for implementing LAM in tensor algebra that runs in time and memory Θ(n log n), significantly improving upon the Θ(n^2) time and memory complexity of traditional attention mechanisms.
For L = ⌈4 log n⌉, Algorithm 1 computes LAM(Q, K, V) in time and memory Θ(n log n).

paper.title: Cluster-Former: Clustering-based Sparse Transformer for Long-Range Dependency Encoding
paper.abstract: Transformer has become ubiquitous in the deep learning field. One of the key ingredients that destined its success is the self-attention mechanism, which allows fully-connected contextual encoding over input tokens. However, despite its effectiveness in modeling short sequences, self-attention suffers when handling inputs with extreme long-range dependencies, as its complexity grows quadratically with respect to the sequence length. Therefore, long sequences are often encoded by Transformer in chunks using a sliding window. In this paper, we propose Cluster-Former, a novel clustering-based sparse Transformer to perform attention across chunked sequences. The proposed framework is pivoted on two unique types of Transformer layer: Sliding-Window Layer and Cluster-Former Layer, which encode local sequence information and global context jointly and iteratively. This new design allows information integration beyond local windows, which is especially beneficial for question answering (QA) tasks that rely on long-range dependencies. Experiments show that Cluster-Former achieves state-of-the-art performance on several major QA benchmarks.

assessments.contribution_summary: Cluster-Former proposes a clustering-based sparse attention mechanism where tokens are grouped by semantic similarity (via K-Means) and attention is applied within clusters, enabling cross-window information flow. This is combined with standard sliding-window local attention layers. The method is designed to capture long-range dependencies beyond local windows, not to restrict attention to local neighborhoods.
assessments.what_remains_open: The gap calls for restricting self-attention to a fixed-size local neighborhood (radius r) in the input sequence to improve computational performance for very long sequences. Cluster-Former does not investigate this direction. Its sliding-window component is a standard baseline technique, not a novel contribution, and the main innovation (Cluster-Former layers) does the opposite — it enables attention across arbitrary distances via clustering. The question of how to design and evaluate local restricted attention (e.g., fixed-window attention with radius r) for large inputs remains entirely open.
